rationale: The mechanism IS the argument: IEEE 754 double-precision arithmetic cannot store 1/3, 1/7, or 1/10 exactly, and the residue of summing N parts back to the unit is produced by the computation rather than illustrated by it. The found object — 0.30000000000000004.com — is a genuinely web-native readymade, and the Duchamp infra-mince / Bochner Measurement lineage is invoked with precision. The chance/order axis is engaged via an inversion worth naming: pure deterministic order (no Math.random) manufactures apparent entropy, because which N yields a closing sum is unpredictable to the eye. Build is minimal, license and attribution are clean, voice is dry-cynic throughout.
reservations: The mechanism is somewhat modest — a slider, a divided bar, and a four-row ledger — and the deeper argument (measurement, infra-mince) is well-trodden DNA territory already mapped by Infra-mince (Enforced), 3 Standard Stoppages, and Measurement: Viewport. P4 is satisfied weakly: the per-visit regeneration is trivial because the arithmetic is deterministic and identical in every conforming browser, so the 'live' aspect is closer to a calculator than to Maleglitch's infinite stream. The surface gag ("computers can't add tenths") is familiar to any developer, so P7's casual-viewer landing carries less surprise than the strongest works in the catalogue.
